A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

systematic uncertainties should always be considered when analysing data from ground-based gamma-ray observatories, and that the traditional summation of ON and OFF-source events is not a suitable technique for the treatment of systematic uncertainties in the combined source analysis.
the joint likelihood approach is the preferred choice for combined source analysis and other applications in the presence of systematic uncertainties.
, in the context of combined source analyses for atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes, joint likelihood techniques should be considered as the preferred method for handling systematic uncertainties.

systematic uncertainties can and should be incorporated in the analysis of Atmospheric Cherenkov data sets, and that doing so is not only possible but straightforward.
